recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes Without Cheese
ingredients_raw: 1 quart whole milk, or as needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Layer 1/3 of the potatoes in the bottom of the prepared baking dish; season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle 3 tablespoons flour over top, then dot with 1/3 of the butter. Repeat layering twice more, then pour in enough milk to fill the dish 3/4 full.

Bake in the preheated oven, checking every 15 minutes, until milk comes to a boil, 45 to 60 minutes. Reduce the heat to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and continue to bake until potatoes are tender, 45 to 60 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Scalloped Potatoes Without Cheese
raw_recipe.description: A quick and easy scalloped potatoes recipe without cheese, just thinly sliced potatoes, whole milk, flour, butter, and seasonings.

review.reviewBody: 10 stars. This is awesome with some minor adjustments. My entire picky family loved these. For serving of four: I used 5-6 small white potatoes (sliced thin) 1 small onion (diced), 5T flour, 5T butter, 2 and 1/4 c milk, 1/2t pepper, 1/2t dry mustard, 1t each of garlic powder, onion powder, paprika and salt, pinch of cayenne pepper and 1/4 c parm cheese. OK grease 2 quart casserole dish, preheat over 425, make roux in saucepan: melt butter then whisk flour cook one minute until it resembles wet sand, add rest and cook until slight thick. put one layer potatoes, one layer onions, one layer sauce and continue once again. Top off with paprika and parm cheese, cook 425 5 minutes then 375 for 50 minutes. Awesome and actually very easy. Must try will not be sorry

like most others have stated, this recipe as it is given is very bland but there are many remedies as suggested by others that make it fab-o!! i will do my best to summarize them all so others behind me don't have to sift through hundreds of reviews...

1.) boil the potatoes for 5 mins beforehand to reduce the cooking time in half
2.) make a roux of the sauce rather than pouring ingredients directly on top. roux is made by mixing flour, butter and milk into sauce pan on medium heat. then add seasonings as you like.
3.) use seasonings to make this recipe really pop. i used 2 cloves garlic, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp celery salt, 1 tbsp chopped onions, a pinch of thyme, a pinch of rosemary, 2 pinches of parsley, 2 pinches of oregano. then at the very last second when the roux was simmering nicely, i added 1/4 cup of shaved parmesan cheese.
4.) once you drain the potatoes, place one layer in the bottom of a 9x13 glass casserole dish, then drizzle 1/3 of the sauce on top. repeat for 2 more layers.
5.) cook covered at 425 degF until the sauce boils and then remov cover and cook at 350 degF for 30 mins.
6.) to get the top of the potatoes browned, you may need to broil them for 5 additional minutes (depending on your oven's cooking capabilities).
7.) voila - enjoy!!!

I loved the way this turned out. I modified it by adding some spices as suggested by other reviews. For 8 person: 1tsp Dry mustard, 2t each of garlic powder, onion powder, paprika and salt, 2 pinches of cayenne pepper. Mix together with the flour in a sauce pan. Slowly stir in butter and milk and hit up. Then after layering the potatoes, layer this flour/spice roux mixture over the potatoes. Sprinkle with parmesan cheese, and repeat layering. YUM!

I made this recipe and added thinly sliced onion on top of each layer of potatoes (my family loves their onions). The end result was a dish that everybody raved about -- no leftovers. I used a mandolin to slice the potatoes so they cooked evenly. And I used a sifter to spread the flour so it too was even. The only issue I had was, the dish bubbled up and over in my stove creating a smoky mess in my oven. Not sure if I had too much milk, although the dish was not soupy when finished. In the future, I will make sure to place the dish on a jellyroll pan in the oven to avoid having any sort of mess to clean up. Thanks for a great recipe that I will definitely make again!

To give this dish a rich depth I used 2 cups of buttermilk and 1 cup 1% milk in a roux for a smaller batch than the recipe called for. Sliced onion, paprika, garlic salt, pepper and parsley made these the best scalloped potatoes I've made.

So good! Creamy yet with crispy edges here and there. I forgot to turn it down after the first 15 minutes so it cooked at 425 degrees for an additional 15 minutes. This gave some of the edges above the milk a nice crispy crunch, a great contrast to the creaminess. Here are my tweaks, which I'll definitely do again:
I layered leftover ham, cut into bite-sized pieces, over the potatoes, then sprinkled 1 tbsp. dried minced onion between the layers, along with 2 tbsp. parmesan cheese. I also sprayed any dry spots of flour with cooking spray to soften the flour. With 15 minutes left I added 3/4 c. shredded cheddar, though gruyere or swiss would have been delicious, too. 
I used only two layers of potatoes instead of three. It was perfect for two people...I had two servings it was so good! (That left 3 for my husband!) 
Next time, instead of adding ham, I'd like to try a smoked sausage or kielbasa.

For serving of four: 5-6 small white potatoes (sliced thin) 1 small onion (diced), 3tbsp flour, 3tbsp butter, 2 and 1/4 c milk, 1/2t pepper, 1/2t dry mustard, 1t each of garlic powder, onion powder, paprika and salt, pinch of cayenne pepper and 1/4 c parm cheese. OK grease 2 quart casserole dish, preheat oven 425, make roux in saucepan. put one layer potatoes, one layer onions, one layer sauce and continue once again. Top off with paprika and parm cheese, cook 425 5 minutes then 375 for 50 minutes.

Hi - This is exactly like my mother's recipe - I made it and used a mandolin to get the potato slices very thin and uniform - also my mother always added breakfast sausages (maple flavor) 12 oz package, you cut each sausage into 3 pieces and add them to each layer - if you have some shredded cheddar cheese hanging out in your freezer this is a great addition in the layers and on top. this makes a great side or whole comfort meal.
Added 1/4 tsp paprika and 1/2 tsp Colmans powdered mustard. This is a good basic recipe. May serve with snipped chives and crumbled bacon.
After reading the reviews I made a simple white sauce using 7 T flour and butter and added a quart of whole milk. I added leftover ham and baked for 1 hour and 40 minutes. Delish!

Great base recipe but followed others’ advice and added spices: garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, paprika, and a pinch of thyme. Made a roux and added in the spice blend before layering among the potatoes
Everyone loved this comfort food dish! Delicious by itself or easier to change with seasonings etc...

Pretty much the recipe that I have used for 50 years with the exception of of adding pepper and diced onion. To speed things up I micro wave on high until it is heated up almost to boil and then pop into oven to continue baking.

My mum and I have been using a recipe the same as this since 1965! My mum made this taken from one of her lovely new American cookbooks when we moved to the USA from the UK. I still have those cookbooks, a set of 12, given with Green Shield stamps I think or whatever the American version of those are. I then sought out the recipe in 1976 when I got married and my children now in their 40's love them too. You must liberally season with salt and pepper between each layer. Tonight I'm making them to go with chicken schnitzel...also love them with a pork chop, steak or roast chicken. Pure comfort food. 😋

This is basically how my whole extended family has made scalloped potatoes, for years. A few tips: definitely liberally salt each layer of potatoes well. Normally I do not like salt but these potatoes definitely need it. Don't forget to add some pepper. To give these potatoes more flavor, add lots of thinly sliced or diced onion to each layer. I use a lot. I also use 2% milk instead of whole milk. I don't know why, but I prefer making scalloped potatoes this way rather than making a cream sauce.
This is the traditional way of cooking scalloped potatoes, if you leave out cheese. If you add cheese to scalloped potatoes, they become potatoes Au gratin or Au gratin potatoes.

2017 Delicious, just like how my Mom and Grandma used to make it! No need to make a béchamel sauce, it defeats the whole purpose. I used gluten free flour rather than wheat and it was just fine; rich and creamy. I did add diced left over ham and some onion powder in the layers. With a veggie or salad on the side, it's a complete meal. This is major comfort food. 10/29/24...The recipe is simple and it's supposed to be! It highlights the natural flavor of potato; no fancy herbs or additives; no pre-made sauce; etc. Just season to your liking with salt pepper, maybe even onion powder. To the low star reviewers, based on your negative comments, you did not execute the recipe as written. Was the dish brought to a boiling point in the oven before reducing the heat? Try it again, folks!
I would suggest grounding old fashioned oats in a blender to replace the flour it comes out amazing. The flour is not a good thing to add to this recipe, but oat flour is better.

If it's scalloped potatoes then of course it doesn't have cheese. The addition of cheese makes them au gratin potatoes. This recipe gives a raw flour taste and lumps. For best results, make a white sauce with a butter and flour roux and milk, lots of salt and pepper and what other seasonings you care to add.
